issues.legal_issue: A writ petition may be maintained to obtain relief against a public authority in a contractual matter when the claim rests on a legal right and corresponding duty and the authority’s conduct is unfair or arbitrary, particularly where deciding the claim does not require interpretation of the contract.
material_facts: The bank was a public sector bank performing public functions and was amenable to writ jurisdiction.
The company sought return of its security documents after its dues had been settled, and the bank’s own account statements showed no outstanding balance.
The relief sought did not require interpretation of contractual terms, and the contract had no arbitration clause.
issues.conclusion: The writ petition was maintainable, and the High Court could issue a mandamus for return of the title deeds.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 12, 14 and 226 of the Constitution, a public authority’s contractual conduct may be reviewed by writ where it is unfair, arbitrary or unreasonable, a legal right and corresponding duty exist, and the circumstances warrant writ relief. Contractual disputes ordinarily belong before a civil court, an arbitral forum or another appropriate forum, and an arbitration clause or effective contractual alternative remedy may be a reason to decline writ jurisdiction. But there is no absolute bar to writ proceedings in contractual matters or merely because facts are disputed. The Court applied ABL International Ltd. v. Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (2004) 3 SCC 553, including its reliance on K.N. Guruswamy v. State of Mysore, D.F.O. v. Ram Sanehi Singh, Gujarat State Financial Corporation v. Lotus Hotels (P) Ltd., LIC of India v. Escorts Ltd., State of U.P. v. Bridge & Roof Co. (India) Ltd., State of Bihar v. Jain Plastics and Chemicals Ltd., Gunwant Kaur v. Municipal Committee, Bhatinda, Century Spg. and Mfg. Co. Ltd. v. Ulhasnagar Municipal Council, and Karnataka State Forest Industries Corporation v. Indian Rocks (2009) 1 SCC 150.

rule.if: contractual_writ_proceeding and public_function_authority and legal_right_with_corresponding_duty and unfair_or_arbitrary_state_action and claim_does_not_require_contract_interpretation and no_contractual_arbitration_clause

predicates.contractual_writ_proceeding: The claimant brought a writ proceeding seeking relief against a public authority in a dispute arising from a contractual relationship.
predicates.public_function_authority: The authority against which relief was sought was a public institution performing public functions.
predicates.legal_right_with_corresponding_duty: The claimant had a legal right to the relief sought and the authority had a corresponding legal duty.
predicates.unfair_or_arbitrary_state_action: The authority acted unfairly or arbitrarily in dealing with the claimant’s asserted right.
predicates.claim_does_not_require_contract_interpre: Deciding the claim did not require interpreting the terms of the contract.
predicates.no_contractual_arbitration_clause: The contract did not provide for arbitration of the dispute.

issues.definition: A contractual writ claim against a public authority is maintainable when the authority performs public functions, the claimant has a corresponding legal right and duty, its conduct is unfair or arbitrary, deciding the claim requires no contract interpretation, and the contract provides no arbitration clause.

issues.legal_issue: A company whose dues to a bank have been settled and whose account records show no outstanding balance is entitled to the return of title deeds held as security for those dues.
material_facts: Another bank paid the company’s outstanding dues to the creditor bank, which accepted and appropriated the payment.
The creditor bank’s account statements showed no outstanding balance.
The company sought return of the title deeds so they could be deposited with its new bank.
issues.conclusion: The company was entitled to the title deeds, and the bank was directed to return them.
issues.legal_principle: A legal right to recover security documents, with a corresponding duty on a public authority to return them, may be enforced under Article 226 where the debt secured by those documents has been settled and the authority’s own records show no outstanding balance. Applying the principles in ABL International Ltd. v. Export Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. (2004) 3 SCC 553 and Karnataka State Forest Industries Corporation v. Indian Rocks (2009) 1 SCC 150, the Court upheld mandamus against the public sector bank in the circumstances of this case.

predicates.writ_claim_for_security_release: A claimant sought return of documents held by a creditor as security for a debt.
predicates.secured_dues_settled: The debt secured by the documents had been paid or otherwise settled.
predicates.creditor_records_nil_balance: The creditor’s account records showed no outstanding balance.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks security documents in a writ proceeding, the secured dues are settled, and the creditor’s records show no balance, the documents must be returned.

issues.legal_issue: The claimant’s entitlement to relief in a writ petition is assessed by reference to the position when the petition was filed, rather than by a liability asserted afterwards.
material_facts: The company filed its writ petition after the creditor bank had received payment settling the dues and had communicated that no dues remained.
The bank relied on an alleged liability arising after the petition was filed through the company’s relationship with other concerns.
issues.conclusion: The date of filing the writ petition was the relevant date for determining the company’s entitlement to relief.
issues.legal_principle: The position existing when a proceeding is instituted is the relevant position for determining the relief sought in that proceeding. The Court relied on Rajahmundry Electric Supply Corporation Ltd. v. A. Nageshwara Rao (1955) 2 SCR 1066.

predicates.writ_proceeding: The claimant brought a writ proceeding seeking relief from a public authority.
predicates.relevant_entitlement_existed_at_filing: The facts supporting the claimant’s entitlement to the requested relief existed when the proceeding was filed.
predicates.later_liability_alleged: The opposing party relied on a liability alleged to have arisen after the proceeding was filed.

issues.definition: When entitlement existed at filing and a later liability is alleged in a writ proceeding, entitlement is assessed by reference to the filing date.
